description_full: CIM Group, Inc. is a non-exchange traded real estate investment trust that elected to be taxed, and operates its business to qualify, as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes beginning with its taxable year ended December 31, 2012. The Company seeks to attain attractive risk-adjusted returns and create long term value for its investors by investing in a diversified portfolio of senior secured mortgage loans, creditworthy long-term net-leased property investments and other senior loan and liquid credit investments. As of September 30, 2025, the Company's loan portfolio consisted of 76 loans with a net book value of 3.2 billion dollars, and investments in real estate-related securities and other of $246.1 million. The Company conducts its commercial real estate lending business through CIM Commercial Lending REIT, a Maryland statutory trust and subsidiary of the Company which the Company expects to be taxed as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes. As of September 30, 2025, CLR holds a diversified portfolio of approximately 1.4 billion dollars which includes first mortgage loans with a net book value of 1.1 billion dollars, commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) with an estimated fair value of 142.7 million dollars, and an investment in the Unconsolidated Joint Venture (as defined in Note 2  Summary of Significant Accounting Policies) with a carrying value of 152.7 million dollars. As of September 30, 2025, the Company owned 198 commercial real estate properties, comprising approximately 6.4 million rentable square feet of commercial space located in 37 states. As of September 30, 2025, the rentable square feet at these properties were 96.9% leased, including month-to-month agreements, if any. As of September 30, 2025, the Company owned condominium developments with a net book value of 17.7 million dollars. CIM Group, Inc. was established in Maryland on July 27, 2010.

financial_summary: CIM REAL ESTATE FIN TR INC is a small-cap real estate business with a $836M market cap on $416M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 76.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin -1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 18.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
